about: Differences between the local QA lab and production that are expected. qa-lab/parity.mjs reports these as explained; any other difference fails the check. Keys are exact (keyPattern only where the object is named by date); platform privileges never take "*". A platform object on one side only is never explained once application code names it. Each reason is repeated in qa-lab/README.md.

differences.reason: Cron jobs are created INACTIVE on purpose; production's definitions (name, schedule, command, user) match exactly. Enable one locally with cron.alter_job(<id>, active := true).
The local image ships only pg_net 0.20.3 (production 0.19.5); its objects live in schema net either way, and its extension row is recorded under schema extensions locally, public in production.

Realtime's daily realtime.messages_YYYY_MM_DD partitions, which only the local Realtime container creates (named by date, so matched by pattern; any other realtime object still fails).
The local pg_cron setup leaves postgres with TRIGGER on cron.job_run_details; production does not. No application object creates a trigger there.
Realtime's own migration bookkeeping table: the local Realtime container grants it differently. The application never reads it.

The lab also seeds a test-mode founding program (two synthetic promised places) so test-mode billing can be exercised; production has a live-mode program only. The live-mode program is compared exactly (promise count and promised places).
